StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDeath.rationale: Right hook. `!wasRemovalPrevented && target == base.Owner && base.Amount > 0` (StockPower.cs:18) maps to powers.py:2972's `creature is not self.owner or self.amount <= 0 -> return`; the replacement carries `StockAmount = base.Amount - 1` (StockPower.cs:23) vs `stock=self.amount - 1` (powers.py:2981) and `ShouldPlaySpawnAnimation = true` vs `respawn=True`; the spawn slot `base.Owner.SlotName` has no sim analogue (slot placement is the monster's record). Checked the 0-amount edge, because power_cmd's step-6 finding (the sim has no 0-amount PowerCmd no-op) would otherwise leave a `Stock(0)` badge the game never shows: monsters/glory/axebot.py:48-51 guards `if stock > 0` exactly as Axebot.cs:78 guards `if (StockAmount > 0)`, so Stock(0) is never applied on either side. The sim's added `self._expire()` matches C#'s CreatureCmd.cs:533 power strip in net effect. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldStopCombatFromEnding.issue: CLOSED. `StockPower.should_stop_combat_from_ending` returns True unconditionally (StockPower.cs:28-31). Found by the command-liveness work rather than by inspection: once `PowerCmd.apply` started honouring `CombatManager.IsEnding` (creature_card_cmds G14 / power_cmd G6), the last Axebot's death made the combat 'ending' and the respawn's own Stock application was refused, so the chain stopped after one link. That is precisely the veto this override exists to provide -- IsEnding consults Hook.ShouldStopCombatFromEnding at CombatManager.cs:196. EXECUTED: test/test_glory.py::TestAxebot::test_stock_respawn_chain.  FIXED 2026-07-28 (round 4). The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-27. THE HOOK NOW EXISTS: `hooks.should_stop_combat_from_ending` (hooks.py:813-824) is the last gate of `CombatState._all_enemies_dead` (combat.py:300-303), mirroring CombatManager.cs:196, and three ported powers use it (AdaptablePower powers.py:3529, SteamEruptionPower :2138, InfestedPower :1495). WHAT REMAINS is that THIS power does not implement it -- an AST scan of powers.py finds no `should_stop_combat_from_ending` on its class -- so it still reaches the same outcome by the mid-death spawn / death-prevention route rather than by the mechanism. Dormant, as before; the trigger is now one line rather than a missing hook.

guards.what: powers.py:2981 passes `combat._rng` for the spawn's HP roll
guards.rationale: The sim passes `combat._rng` -- the shared LEGACY random.Random -- to the spawned monster's constructor (powers.py:2981), and Monster.__init__ rolls the spawn's HP from it (monsters/base.py:78-79 `hp = rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)`), where the game rolls a mid-combat spawn's HP on a NAMED stream. Half A found seven power units reaching for `combat._rng` where C# names a stream, so this was checked as a systematic class rather than trusted: the sim REPAIRS it one level up. `CreatureCmd.add` calls `combat.assign_parity_hp(creature)` (cmds.py:254 -> combat.py:259-267), which re-rolls a mid-combat spawn's HP on the **Niche** stream against the current siblings, mirroring CombatState.CreateCreature's SetUniqueMonsterHpValue -- and it is a no-op in legacy mode, where the shared rng IS the model. The Axebot really does have HP variance (min_hp 70, max_hp 78), so the repair is load-bearing rather than vacuous. Faithful, with the caveat that the constructor's `randint` still consumes a draw from the unseeded shared rng in parity mode -- harmless, because no parity content reads that stream. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

`wasRemovalPrevented: true` is passed when Hook.ShouldDie returned FALSE, i.e. when the DEATH was prevented (CreatureCmd.cs:566), and `false` on the real-death path (CreatureCmd.cs:519) -- the parameter is misnamed in the decompiled source and is NOT about ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath (computed separately at CreatureCmd.cs:508). So `!wasRemovalPrevented` means "the creature actually died". The sim fires hooks.on_death ONLY on the should_die-returned-True branch (cmds.py:98-105) and fires nothing on the prevented branch, so the guard is satisfied structurally. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

Slot placement is presentation/layout in the sim's model; the Ovicopter egg-slot finding shows the sim DOES model list POSITION where it matters for targeting, and CreatureCmd.add appends here. Flagged as a waiver rather than a gap because a single-enemy replacement lands in the same list position either way.
